rule: Each row is one published figure for Manchester, Cheltenham or Bristol. There is no UK-wide yield in this file. An average is the unweighted mean of the rows marked for that place and asset, and only where at least two rows qualify. Asking quotes are not mixed with completed sales. A gross yield (rent divided by price) is not a net initial yield. Agent market views are not put into an average.

rows.location: St James House, St James Square, Cheltenham
rows.source: Consorto listing, last updated 24 October 2026, repeating the selling agent’s particulars
rows.notes: The page title does not print the building name. It describes a freehold Grade A office in St James Square of 82,843 sq ft NIA, let to seven tenants including BPE Solicitors, Barnett Waddingham, Crowe U.K. and Amwins, passing rent £2,088,309. Those facts match St James House. Offers in excess of £20,000,000, reflecting a net initial yield of 9.8% if purchaser’s costs are 6.80%. This is the vendor’s asking quote on this asset. It is not a completed sale and it is not the area average.

rows.source: Punchline Gloucestershire, 23 July 2025, quoting KBW Property Consultants
rows.notes: Offers of £950,000 for about 3,450 sq ft multi-let offices. Passing rent £54,275 a year. A purchase at that price is stated to reflect a net initial yield of 5.4% after purchaser’s costs of 5.7%. Much smaller than the town-centre towers. Asking, not a completed sale.

rows.source: Gloucestershire Live, 29 June 2023, and a Consorto page still showing the same guide when read on 1 November 2026
rows.notes: Gloucestershire Live names Eagle Tower, 15 storeys, over 81,000 sq ft, on the market at £18 million, and says the advert quoted a net initial yield of 8.5%. Consorto shows 81,190 sq ft, 15 storeys, £18,000,000, net yield 8.52% and NOI £1,533,600, without printing the name (https://www.consorto.com/properties/16644-office-for-sale-in-cheltenham-united-kingdom-freehold-investment-opportunity-b-class, page last updated 7 September 2026). Punchline reported in 2026 that the owning company was sold on 2 June 2026; that report does not give a property yield. The 8.52% figure is an asking quote and may be stale.

rows.location: 15-storey multi-let office, Cheltenham town centre (building not named)
rows.source: Avison Young, LinkedIn post by Calum Jackson, 27 November 2025
rows.notes: Offers in excess of £15,000,000, net initial yield 11.22% assuming purchaser’s costs of 6.73%, 89,050 sq ft, net income £1,796,015. The post does not name the building. Eagle Tower is the town’s 15-storey office and was previously offered around £18 million, so this may be a later guide for the same tower. Left out of the average so the tower is not counted twice.

Regional Office Property Unit Trust exchanged unconditional contracts to buy St James House for £21.8 million, reflecting a net initial yield of 7.5%. About 81,731 sq ft, seven tenants. This is a completed sale of the same building, five years before the 2026 asking quote. One sale is not an area average. Also reported by The Business Magazine on 2 February 2021.

rows.source: Savills Regional Office Investment Market Watch, May 2026, and the July 2026 update
rows.notes: BNY bought its own regional headquarters for £114 million, 200,000 sq ft, yield 6.86%. Savills dates the note May 2026; the July 2026 note repeats the same price and yield. BNP Paribas Real Estate’s Q1 2026 Big 10 report states about 6.9% and £114 million for the same deal; 6.86% is the figure used here. This is an owner-occupier purchase, not evidenced as a multi-let investment sale.

rows.asset_type: Office — completed sale, letting not stated
rows.source: Savills Regional Office Investment Market Watch, 31 July 2026
rows.notes: Northtree Investment Management bought the 110,000 sq ft building, completed in 2021, for £55 million, reflecting a yield of 6.80%. Savills does not say whether it was multi-let. H1 2026 sale. The report date is 31 July 2026.

rows.location: Multi-let office near Manchester Airport (address not published)
rows.notes: Offers in excess of £16,000,000, reflecting a net initial yield of 11.10% after full purchaser’s costs. 90,154 sq ft, near the airport, not the city centre. The page header also shows 11.00%; the 11.10% sentence is used. One asking quote is not an area average.

rows.source: BNP Paribas Real Estate, UK Big 10 Regional Office Market, Q1 2026
rows.notes: Table: £66 million, £374 per sq ft, yield 8.00%, buyer Lloyds, vendor KFIM. The commentary says about 8% on about eight years’ income. Savills’ May 2026 note reports the same sale at £65 million and 8.2%. The two published figures disagree, so neither is used in an average.

rows.source: Savills Regional Office Investment Market Watch, May 2026
rows.notes: Lloyds Bank acquired 10 Canons Way for £65 million, reflecting a yield of 8.2%. Savills describes this in its note on owner-occupiers. BNP reports £66 million and 8.00% for the same building. Not averaged.

rows.location: Multi-let office in Bristol city centre (address not published)
rows.notes: Offers in excess of £5,460,000, net initial yield 9.00%. 18,731 sq ft, refurbished 2020, four tenants, 69% occupied, leasehold with 114 years remaining. The address is behind a login. One asking quote is not an area average.
